key_insight: Plateau elasticity in regiorandom poly(3-alkylthiophenes) is dominated by reversible interchain associations rather than uniquely indicating topological entanglement.
engineering_relevance: Tuning interchain association strength and lifetime offers a route to controlling stress relaxation, viscoelasticity, and processability in conjugated polymers.
method: Use regiorandom poly(3-alkylthiophenes) as a model system.
Compare plateau relaxation with segmental and terminal dynamics.
Probe responses to mechanical perturbation and side-chain length.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports Arrhenius plateau relaxation decoupled from segmental and terminal dynamics, persistent reorganization under mechanical perturbation, and systematic side-chain-length dependence.
watch_item: The results support associations consistent with π–π interactions, but the abstract does not establish their microscopic origin definitively or demonstrate generality across conjugated polymers.
paper_title: Reversible Interchain Associations Dominate Plateau Elasticity in Conjugated Polymers
